lead: An addressing mode is the rule that tells the CPU where an operand is. A memory map is the address plan that says which addresses hold code, data, stack and registers. These two ideas must match: the addressing mode decides how an address is formed; the memory map decides what that address means. In the 8051, PIC and ARM, the same instruction mnemonic can use different modes. Read the mode and the map together, or the operand comes from the wrong place. Firmware, drivers, boot code and exam questions all depend on this.
prereq: You need: register names and bus widths from Chapter 2.1, Chapter 2.2 and Chapter 2.3.

blocks.text: An addressing mode is the rule for finding an operand, the value an instruction acts on. The rule produces an effective address (EA), the final address used for a memory operand. The mode can take the operand from the instruction bits, from a register, or from memory. The memory map is the address plan: it assigns ranges to code, data, stack, registers and I/O. The mode chooses the space; the map says what sits at the address.

Six operand kinds repeat across families. Immediate data is inside the instruction. A register operand names a register. A direct address is a number that points into a memory space. An indirect operand uses a register as a pointer, so the pointer's contents are the address. An indexed operand adds a base and an index to reach a table. A relative operand adds a signed offset to the program counter (PC). Some syllabi call indexed addressing based addressing. Pointer addressing usually means indirect addressing.

Use both ideas together. In the 8051, address 30H in internal RAM is a data byte; address 0030H in code memory is an instruction byte. An instruction such as MOV A,30H uses direct data addressing. An instruction such as MOVC A,@A+DPTR uses indexed code addressing. If you read only the number, you may fetch from the wrong space.

The 8051 has separate code and data spaces. Code memory starts at 0000H, the reset vector, and the basic 8051 has 4 KB on chip, 0000H-0FFFH. Internal data RAM is 00H-7FH, 128 bytes. Special function registers (SFRs) occupy 80H-FFH and include ACC at E0H, PSW at D0H, and DPTR split as DPH 83H and DPL 82H. The stack lives in internal RAM and grows upward. Direct addresses below 80H mean RAM; addresses 80H and above mean SFRs.

Indirect @Ri uses R0 or R1 as an 8-bit pointer. In the basic 8051 it reaches internal RAM 00H-7FH. MOVX @Ri reaches external data memory. Indexed @A+DPTR and @A+PC read code memory; MOVC is the usual table lookup. The bit mode reaches bit-addressable RAM 20H-2FH and bit-addressable SFRs. Relative mode is used by jumps and adds an 8-bit signed offset to the PC.

sections.h3: PIC and ARM: banks and one flat space

blocks.text: The PIC16F877A is Harvard: program memory stores 14-bit instructions and data memory is separate. Program memory has reset vector 0000H and interrupt vector 0004H. Data memory is banked; the STATUS register bits RP1:RP0 select one of four banks, each 128 bytes. Direct addressing uses a 7-bit address plus those bank bits. Indirect addressing uses INDF as the window; the actual data-memory address is formed from FSR and the IRP bit in STATUS (STATUS<7>).

PIC modes are immediate (literal in the instruction), direct (7-bit file address plus bank bits), indirect through FSR/INDF, and absolute GOTO/CALL using an 11-bit address plus PCLATH page bits. Computed jumps write PCL; there is no general PC-relative branch/call offset mode. The bank bits are part of the effective address, not an optional extra.

ARM has one 32-bit address space for code, data, stack and I/O. The vector table sits at low addresses: reset at 0000H, undefined at 0004H, SWI at 0008H, prefetch abort at 000CH, data abort at 0010H, IRQ at 0018H and FIQ at 001CH. The PC is visible as R15 and reads ahead because of the pipeline; a PC-relative address uses the PC value plus an offset.

ARM modes include immediate (a constant encoded in the instruction), register, shifted register (a barrel shifter scales or shifts one operand), PC-relative, pre-indexed and post-indexed load/store, and stack forms. Pre-indexed LDR R0,[R1,#4] forms R1+4 and loads; add ! to write the new address back to R1. Post-indexed LDR R0,[R1],#4 loads from R1, then sets R1=R1+4. Full descending stack: STMFD sp!,{r0-r3} pushes; LDMFD sp!,{r0-r3} pops.

figure.caption: The 8051 keeps code, internal RAM and SFR space separate. Notice R0=30H points to data RAM 30H=5AH, while DPTR=1000H plus A=00H points to code 1000H=7BH.

spec.title: 8051 memory map and operand paths
spec.aria: The block map shows 8051 code, data RAM and SFR space, with R0=30H pointing to RAM 30H=5AH and DPTR=1000H pointing to code 1000H=7BH.

examples.question: Before each instruction A = 00H, R0 = 30H, internal RAM 30H = 5AH, DPTR = 1000H, and code memory 1000H = 7BH. Find A after (a) MOV A,@R0 and (b) MOVC A,@A+DPTR. Give both hex and decimal.
steps: The indirect symbol @R0 uses 30H as the data-memory address. Internal RAM 30H holds 5AH.
MOV A,@R0 copies 5AH into A. So A = 5AH = 90 decimal.
(b) MOVC uses code memory. A = 00H and DPTR = 1000H.
Code memory 1000H holds 7BH. MOVC copies it into A. So A = 7BH = 123 decimal.
examples.check:
a = int('5A', 16)
b = int('7B', 16)
print(a)
print(b)

traps: Direct address is not immediate data: MOV A,30H loads RAM 30H; MOV A,#30H loads the constant 30H.
@R0 uses the contents of R0, not the address of R0. If R0=30H, @R0 points to RAM 30H.
MOVC reads code memory, not data RAM; MOVX is for external data. Do not mix the two.
PIC bank bits RP1:RP0 in STATUS select the data bank. A correct 7-bit address in the wrong bank reads the wrong byte.
ARM pre-indexed writeback changes the base register only with !. Post-indexed writes back the updated address to the base register.

quiz.q: Define addressing mode and memory map.
quiz.a: An addressing mode is the rule for finding an operand and forming its effective address. A memory map is the address plan that assigns ranges to code, data, stack, registers and I/O.
Indirect data addressing: R0 holds the data-memory address of the operand. If R0=30H, @R0 points to internal RAM 30H.

quiz.q: Why does the 8051 keep separate code and data spaces?
quiz.a: It is a Harvard-style split: code is fetched from program memory and data is read or written in RAM/SFRs. The same address number can be a code byte or a data byte, so MOVC is used for code tables and MOV for data.

quiz.q: Before MOV A,@R1, A=00H, R1=40H, and RAM 40H=3CH. What is A after?
quiz.a: R1=40H is the pointer; RAM 40H holds 3CH; MOV A,@R1 copies 3CH into A, so A=3CH.

quiz.q: ARM LDR R2,[R3,#8]! with R3=0x1000 and memory at 0x1008 = 0x55. Find R2 and R3.
quiz.a: Pre-indexed with writeback: address = 0x1000 + 8 = 0x1008; R2 = 0x55; R3 becomes 0x1008.

quiz.q: PIC direct address 25H is used with STATUS RP1:RP0 = 01. Which data-memory address is reached?
quiz.a: RP1:RP0=01 selects bank 1. Bank 1 starts at 80H, so 25H maps to 80H+25H=0A5H. The operand is at data memory 0A5H.

quiz.q: 8051: DPTR=0100H, A=05H, code memory 0105H=C0H. After MOVC A,@A+DPTR, what is A and why?
quiz.a: EA = DPTR + A = 0100H + 05H = 0105H. MOVC reads code memory, not data RAM. Code byte 0105H is C0H, so A=C0H.

beyond: Not for the exam. RISC-V adds a small, regular set of addressing modes and is now common in teaching and industry. Position-independent code uses PC-relative addressing so a program can run at any load address. An MMU adds page tables that translate virtual to physical addresses, so the memory map seen by code is not the physical map. Linker scripts place code, data and stack in named regions. Search for RISC-V addressing modes, ARM AAPCS stack rules, linker script MEMORY, and MMU page table walk.
